## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `94dbce5d54ed0221df061522e06babc96463e35c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: AGENTS.md + scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs

### ① Derived judgments

- Head `94dbce5d54ed0221df061522e06babc96463e35c` is one commit on `f81e4b6c`, which is `main` as read for this review (the merge base equals `main`). Net diff: 2 files, +17 −5: `AGENTS.md` (+1 −1, line 306) and `scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs` (+16 −4: the helper's docblock and condition, the N-a row's argv, one new self-test row). Both files are the surface of claim 6899846531; nothing else is touched. The dev report 6900121433 names the same head, files and counts.
- M4 holds. Line 306 now reads "CODEOWNERS routes every Tier H surface but the low-risk arm's rows to the approvers".
  - Against `.github/CODEOWNERS` at this head: the routed Tier H lines are `/AGENTS.md`, `/CLAUDE.md`, `/docs/NORTH-STAR.md`, `/.github/workflows/` and the five `ui/` rows (`/ui/docs/adr/` among them). There is no `/docs/adr/`, `/skills/` or `/ui/skills/` line.
  - Against the arm's rows as the queue guard reads them: the guard's own mirror assertion holds `armPatterns` to `/docs/adr/,/skills/,/ui/skills/`, read off the register's `lowRisk` rows (`adr` carries `lowRisk` with `addOnly: true`; `ui-adr` carries none). The set CODEOWNERS leaves out is exactly the set the sentence names, so the sentence is true, and `ui/docs/adr/**` is correctly still routed.
  - The term resolves inside the directive: line 292 names "skills-only wording and add-only ADR notes (`lowRiskArmVerdict`)".
  - Budget: the line is 118 bytes, all ASCII, under the 120-byte cap; AGENTS.md stays at 1050 lines.
  - Other rules-face sentences: `AGENTS.md` names CODEOWNERS on line 306 only. `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/**` names it three times (SKILL.md line 162, `references/lanes/skills.md` line 8, `references/triage-duties.md` line 93), each as a lane or duty entry, none saying what it routes. In the `.github/CODEOWNERS` header the two sentences that name the arm's rows are right ("the two skills catalogs and the root ADR tree ... has NO line here"; "less the low-risk arm's `/docs/adr/` and `/skills/` rows"). Its title line still generalises to "every Tier H governed surface", qualified lower in the same header: see N3.
- S7 holds, read on the text and not run.
  - The trace. In the sweep `readArmLanding` hands the guard `armGit`, which records every read that throws. `catalogFilesOf` sends two `diff-tree` shapes: the status read (`-r --no-commit-id --no-renames --raw -z -m --first-parent SHA`) and, for a modified file under the add-only row, the patch read built by `addOnlyDiffArgv(['diff-tree', '-p', '--no-commit-id', '-m', '--first-parent'], [sha], path)`. When only the patch read throws, `catalogFilesOf` carries `patch: null`, the arm reads H, and `armUnreadInputs` lists the one failed read. `armSettledWithoutUnread` asks `favourableArmGitRead` for that argv; it carries `-p` and no `--raw`, so the answer is null and the function returns null before any re-read. `readArmLanding` then returns `not-measured` with "the low-risk arm could not read `git diff-tree -p` ...". Before this head the same argv was answered with a status listing, `addOnlyNoteReasons` read it as "shows no hunk", and the landing came back `tier-h`.
  - Other argv shapes. Inside `readLowRiskTier` the guard sends exactly those two `diff-tree` shapes; the `--name-only` reads belong to the row enumeration and never pass through `armGit`. The status read keeps its favourable answer (it carries `--raw`, not `-p`). The row `#33765-N-f` still records the argv the guard really sends on the default fixture and requires a non-null answer for each, so a renamed status read reds there.
  - The N-a row edit is forced: with the new condition the bare `['diff-tree', LANDED]` gets null, and the old `.includes(...)` on it would throw. The edit adds `'--raw'` to that argv and changes nothing else. The row still pins what it pinned: null for `rev-parse`, a clean changeset for `show`, a modified-file listing naming the path for the status read. It is not weaker; the live spelling is held by N-f and by the new row's third conjunct.
  - The new row `#33539-S7` has three conjuncts: the end-to-end read (an ADR path, the patch read alone throwing, the result `not-measured` naming `git diff-tree`), null for the real patch argv, non-null for the real status argv. Under the pre-fix condition the second conjunct turns false at once, and the first does too by the trace above (the fixture sends no other read that could fail). The row is ablation-sensitive. The dev reports the same ablation red on exactly this row; this review did not re-run it.
  - The battery `#33603` goes from 62 to 63 assertions against a declared floor of 51. The roster's rule is a floor, not an equality, so no roster edit is owed.
- S8 holds. The 维护者速读 "风险与回滚" bullet says that with the `/docs/adr/` line gone, a root ADR pull opened ready or readied by hand no longer gets GitHub's code-owner request, and that for every ADR change other than an add-only note the queue guard (refused without a `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` approval) and the relay's per-pull request to both approvers hold the ruling. That matches CODEOWNERS at this head, `catalogFilesOf` (an unread or non-add-only ADR diff reads H) and the relay behaviour that record 6898480793 read on #33975.
- Check-runs on this head are NOT a verdict yet (read 2026-11-15T19:42Z): 12 success, 23 skipped, 11 still running: `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Test Core (1/8)`, `Test Core (2/8)`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · source gates`. Green so far include `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Check Changeset`, `Type Check · workspace`. The leg that runs this file's self-test (`Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`) is among those still running, so the 863-assertion figure and the new row's green are the dev's reading until it closes. This verdict is on the text; it does not stand in for a green roll-up.
- This round was read, not run. Nothing was built, and no self-test, gate or ablation was re-run.

### ② Semver level

None. No published package is touched: a rules file and a PM script. `skip-changeset` is on the PR and is right. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are on the PR body, match claim 6899846531, and are right: no published schema, no metadata key, no narrowing.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Tier H handling. The PR touches `AGENTS.md`, so it is governed and lands at Tier H; `scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs` is also an enforcement-chain row in CODEOWNERS. The PR is a draft, auto-merge is not armed, it carries no review, and nothing in the diff readies it, relaxes a guard or touches `GOVERNED_APPROVERS`. It stays draft until an authorized approval. This record is the seat's review of record, ⛔ not an approval.
- Deviation 1, the N9 hunk of commit `3bc27d49` left out. Answered: leaving it out is right. That hunk (+7 −4) only re-wraps two header comments of `.github/CODEOWNERS` and adds "in the root tree" and "under the low-risk arm's conditions". `.github/CODEOWNERS` is outside the claimed surface and the claim says stop on breach. Nothing is owed in this PR. The nit itself stays open with no carrier: see N3.
- Deviation 2, the branch restarted as a plain push from `main` after #33975's branch was deleted. Answered: confirmed, one commit on current `main`, no force, the same ref name as #33975's implementation branch.
- Human Minimum item 3 is left unticked with its reason (`pnpm lint` not run; no package source changed). Answered: acceptable; `Lint · ESLint` on this head is still running and decides it.
- `open_questions` is empty. No out-of-scope note beyond the two deviations.
- SQL push-down: n/a.

### ④ Design judgment

- `AGENTS.md` against the code it cites: the reworded clause agrees with CODEOWNERS and with the guard's mirror on this head, as in ①. It closes M4 of record 6898480793.
- `scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs` against the contract it implements (#33765 N-a: a reason from a stand-in answer never settles Tier H): the helper now has no answer for the patch read, so the sweep no longer reports a measured Tier H on a patch it did not read. The direction is the safe one: the landing is listed with the maintainer's merges and the sweep reads INCOMPLETE. The queue, the relay and `--pr` are unchanged; there an unread ADR diff reads H. It closes S7.

Findings:

N1 (nit) — the null answer is wider than the defect. An ADR landing whose patch read fails and which also carries a measured Tier H reason of its own (a `security` label, a `Clause-②: yes` body, a path outside the allowlist) now reads NOT MEASURED, where N-a's rule would let the measured reason settle it. That errs toward INCOMPLETE and never toward a false complete, and it is what the card ordered. The helper's docblock says "no stand-in patch is favourable" without showing it, and the `readArmLanding` docblock still states N-a without this exception. One clause there would do.

N2 (nit) — the two halves of the new condition are pinned only together. Both shapes the guard sends differ in both flags, so dropping either `argv.includes('--raw')` or `!argv.includes('-p')` alone turns no row red. The bare argv the N-a row used to send is the missing case: `favourableArmGitRead(['diff-tree', LANDED], [SK]) === null` beside the edited conjunct would pin the `--raw` half.

N3 (nit, off this card's surface) — #33975's N9 has no carrier. The `.github/CODEOWNERS` header still says an add-only note "rides the low-risk arm" without "root tree" or "under the arm's conditions", its two added lines still run past the wrap width, and its title line still reads "every Tier H governed surface" although three arm rows have no line. Each is qualified lower in the same header and the guard refuses whatever the comment over-reads, so nothing is wrong at the gate. The PR body's "Not carried" names N9 but no card holds it; fold it into the next card that opens that file.

No must-fix, no should-fix, three nits (N1 to N3). M4, S7 and S8 of record 6898480793 are closed on this head.
